producer_report.summary: The producer brief now has a "Words you must not write" section before the Checks section. It lists the 17 boundary-scan words and 6 fragments. It says the scan is whole-word and case-insensitive, and that singular, plural and hyphenated forms are listed. The list lives in athena-context (`briefs::boundary_words` and `briefs::boundary_fragments`), built from fragments, so no tracked file contains a banned term. xtask keeps its own scanner list. A new test in `xtask/tests/policy.rs` fails if the two lists differ. That needed athena-context as an xtask dev-dependency only. The dependency-direction test counts normal dependencies only, so docs/architecture.md is unchanged. Cargo.lock gained the one edge. Other edits: a pointer line in `prompts/producer.md`, the M19 row in `docs/enforcement.md`, decision D73 in `docs/decisions.md`, and a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. The scanner, the reader and verifier briefs, and records/ are untouched.

checks_run.note: all pass, including athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where, the new the_producer_brief_lists_exactly_the_scanners_terms, dependency_direction_matches_the_architecture, and every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists

open_issues: Two copies of the word list still exist (athena-context and xtask), tied by a test rather than merged. Making the scanner read the brief's list would be a separate change to the rule's mechanism.
The brief now shows the producer the banned terms. This is the point of the request, but a producer could still copy one. The scan stays the backstop.
The 150-token cost in D73 is an estimate, not a measurement.
mistakes: I tried grep through Bash and the hook denied it; I switched to the Grep tool.
learnings: The M21 test (`actual()` in xtask/tests/policy.rs) keeps only normal dependencies (kind null), so dev-dependencies between workspace crates do not need an entry in docs/architecture.md.
The M19 scan reads working-tree files from the tracked-file list, so edits to tracked files are scanned before commit.
Prompt text has a token budget test (the_contract_is_within_its_budget); the one added line in producer.md stayed within it.
The Bash hook rejects grep, so only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm run there.
